title: Undo drawer: Proof strip
summary: Stack history. Return the whole list.
descriptionMd:
Inputs
`readings` is a list of integers (numbers with no decimal part). It may be empty, and numbers may repeat unless task 1 says otherwise.

Your tasks
1. Create a list `stack`. Use a stack, which is a pile where you add and remove items only at the top. Read `readings` from left to right. A number of 0 or more adds that number to the top. A negative number tells you how many top items to remove: -3 means remove up to three items. Stop if the stack becomes empty. `stack` is the final stack, from bottom to top.
2. Complete `undoDrawerProofStrip` so it returns `stack`. Return it, do not print it.

Example
If `readings` is [8, 10, -8, 5, 5], then `stack` is [5, 5] and `undoDrawerProofStrip` returns [5, 5].

Rules
- If `stack` is empty, return [].

Test data
TEST DATA 1: `readings` is [-8, 0, 13, 18, 18].
TEST DATA 2: `readings` is [9, -3, 9, 9].

constraints: Answers fit in a signed 32-bit integer: -2,147,483,648 through 2,147,483,647.
Input numbers have no decimal part. They range from -1,000,000 to 1,000,000. Follow any extra input rules in task 1.
Efficiency goal: time O(n); extra memory, including the helper list, O(n). n is the input length. These labels describe how work and memory grow with the input.
